summary: The draft cites only five classical cover-time sources. Two gaps matter: the Matthews comparator in the main table has no citation and the (4/27)n^3 upper bound is credited to Feige's lower-bound paper; the positioning and discussion text also refers to family-specific cover-time asymptotics without citing any.
missing_literatures: Feige tight upper bound on cover time
family-specific cover-time asymptotics (random regular, Erdos-Renyi, 2D grid/torus)

rewrite_targets.reason: The Matthews-type reference (max hitting time x H_{n-1}) is a comparator in Table 2 and is described in Background (Graph-aware characterizations) and Method (Compared predictors) with no citation. The (4/27)n^3 'Feige upper bound', the paper's primary best-bound comparator, is cited only to Feige1995ATL, whose title is 'A Tight Lower Bound on the Cover Time'. The same misattribution appears in the Introduction, Background, Design rationale and Discussion. A reviewer checking comparator provenance would catch both problems.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: Matthews' method bounds the cover time by the maximum hitting time times $H_{n-1}$. / Feige's upper bound $\tfrac{4}{27}n^3+o(n^3)$ is the exact worst case
search_topics: Matthews covering problems for Markov chains
Feige a tight upper bound on the cover time for random walks on graphs
Levin Peres Wilmer Markov chains and mixing times cover time Matthews method

rewrite_targets.reason: The Positioning paragraph says prior work derives 'asymptotics for specific families' but cites none. The Discussion then relies on such results without citations: random 3-regular and dense Erdos-Renyi graphs sit in the near-n ln n regime, and grid cover time may not follow a single power law. One to three citations for random-regular, random-graph and 2D-torus cover-time asymptotics would ground these statements and the choice of evaluated families. The story does not need to change.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: it derives bounds that hold for all graphs, or asymptotics for specific families
